message: Cannot find the type '{0}' of assembly '{1}' in the project or its references. Use the reflection name of the type: separate nested types with '+', and write generic types with a backtick followed by the number of type parameters, for example 'System.Collections.Generic.List`1'.
rationale: The message gives no way forward although the most common cause is an incorrect type name passed to TypeFactory.GetType(string), which expects a reflection (metadata) name. The assembly placeholder is empty on that path.
codeChange: ReflectionMapper.GetNamedTypeSymbolByMetadataName (ReflectionMapper.cs:79) passes assemblyName?.ToString(), which is null when the call comes from DeclarationFactory.GetTypeByReflectionName (TypeFactory.GetType(string)), so the message reads "of assembly ''". Use a separate message without the assembly in that case, or pass a value such as 'any referenced assembly'.
